chapter: Early life and training in Boston
title: Birth in Boston, Everett childhood and his parents
summary: Whaley was born in Boston in 1892 and raised in Everett; he recalls a burglary scare, names his parents, and describes his father's Virginia family and supposed Indian ancestry.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was born in Boston at the corner of Church and Melrose in 1892. And my father and mother moved to Boston after six months of living there, I mean to Everett, Massachusetts. It's about six or seven miles from Boston, just like from New York to Brooklyn. And well, the first thing I remember was in 1895 the subway opened and my mother and father went on the opening ride and the burglars broke in the house and my sister put us all in a room and told us to keep still and I think something
scared the burglars away because they never come in the house. Then that was when I was about three years old, and when I was seven years old my mother decided to give me piano lessons.

James Thomas Whaley. And my mother was born in Richmond, Virginia and he was born in Fairfax County of West Virginia. I believe my father was an Indian because I went down there in 1902 and I saw this great big giant and my father said that was his father and he was a red man and he was a blacksmith and he could life a horse. That was in 1902 when we went down there.
